key_features.classic_presentation: IBD flare presents with crampy abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, urgency, and weight loss. Chronic/recurrent pattern. Extraintestinal manifestations (arthritis, eye inflammation) may occur. Known IBD history typical but can be new diagnosis.
key_features.typical_demographics: Peak onset 15-30 years. Northern latitudes, Caucasians, Ashkenazi Jews higher risk. Family history common.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Chronic immune-mediated inflammation of GI tract. Crohn's: transmural, any GI location. UC: mucosal, colon only.

diagnostic_questions.context: Bloody diarrhea is hallmark of UC. Less common in Crohn's. Distinguishes from IBS.
IBD is chronic disease with relapses. Not acute first-time presentation typically.
Severe flares: >6 BM/day. UC flares can have 10-20+ bloody stools daily.

expected_positive_responses: feeling like need to go but nothing
diagnostic_questions.context: Urgency and tenesmus are characteristic of UC.
Unintentional weight loss common in active disease.

red_flags.finding: Severe abdominal distension with no BM
red_flags.action: Toxic megacolon - life-threatening, needs emergency surgery
Severe flare or complication - urgent hospitalization

typical_management: Corticosteroids for flares, biologics (anti-TNF), immunomodulators. Severe: hospitalization, IV steroids. Surgical consultation if complications.
disposition: Mild-moderate: outpatient with GI follow-up. Severe: hospital admission. Complications: emergency department.
patient_education: IBD is chronic intestinal inflammation. Flares require treatment intensification. With proper management, most achieve remission. Urgent care needed for severe symptoms.
